hero.title: Find answers fast
hero.body: Search common seller problems and follow short step-by-step guides. If you still need a person, use Contact.

noResults.title: No matching guides
noResults.body: Try different words, or send us a note and we will point you the right way.

delete-account.title: How to delete your Stallio account
delete-account.excerpt: Permanently remove your shop, products, orders, and messages from Settings.
delete-account.intro: Deleting your account removes your shop and dashboard data. This cannot be undone from the product. Sign in first.
steps: Sign in at stallio.shop/login and open your seller dashboard.
Go to Settings in the dashboard sidebar.
Scroll to Delete Account and choose Delete My Account.
In the confirmation box, type DELETE MY ACCOUNT exactly, then confirm.
When deletion finishes, you are signed out and returned to the home page.

restore-account.title: Recover a deleted Stallio account
restore-account.excerpt: Deletion is permanent in the product. Contact support if you need to ask about recovery.
restore-account.intro: Account deletion is designed to be permanent. There is no self-serve restore button after you confirm DELETE MY ACCOUNT.
steps: Check whether you can still sign in at stallio.shop/login. If login works, the account was not deleted.
If login fails and you already deleted the account, open the Contact page.
Use a clear subject such as Account recovery and include the email and shop username you used.
Explain when you deleted the account and why you need it back.
Wait for a reply. Recovery is not guaranteed and depends on what data is still available on our side.

account-suspended.title: Why an account can be suspended
account-suspended.excerpt: Shop or dashboard access may pause for non-payment, abuse, or risk to other users.
account-suspended.intro: Stallio can suspend a shop, the seller dashboard, or both. You may see a message that dashboard access is suspended when you try to sign in or open the dashboard.
steps: Common reasons include unpaid subscription fees, abuse, illegal or harmful shop content, or risk to other users, as described in the Terms of Service.
If only the dashboard is blocked, your public shop may still behave differently than a full account close.
Check the email inbox for the address on your Stallio account for a suspension or billing note from us.
Review Pricing and your last payment status if the issue may be billing related.
Use the after-suspension guide for what to do next, including how to contact support.

after-suspension.title: What to do after a suspension
after-suspension.excerpt: Contact support with context, fix billing if needed, and ask for a review.
after-suspension.intro: There is no automatic unsuspend button. Clear the cause when you can, then ask the team to review your account.
steps: Read any email Stallio sent about the suspension and note the reason if one is given.
If the issue is billing, resolve the unpaid plan or failed payment first when you can.
If you can still open the dashboard, use Support Chat with Admin and describe what happened.
If you cannot open the dashboard, use the Contact page. Include your account email, shop username, and a short explanation or appeal.
Do not create a second account to bypass a suspension. Wait for a human reply before changing shop content that was flagged.

login-issues.title: Fix common login problems
login-issues.excerpt: Check email, password, verification, and suspension before assuming the account is gone.
login-issues.intro: Most sign-in problems come from the wrong email, a forgotten password, an unverified email, or a suspended dashboard.
steps: Open stallio.shop/login and confirm you are using the same email you used at signup.
If the password fails, use Forgot Password and follow the reset email.
If you never finished email verification, open the verification link from your signup email or request a new one from the verify-email flow.
If you see a message that dashboard access is suspended, follow the suspension guides instead of repeatedly trying passwords.
Still stuck? Use Contact with the email you think belongs to the account.

reset-password.title: Reset your password
reset-password.excerpt: Use Forgot Password, open the email link, and set a new password.
reset-password.intro: You can reset a seller password without knowing the old one, as long as you can access the account email inbox.
steps: Go to stallio.shop/forgot-password.
Enter the email on your Stallio account and submit.
Open the inbox for that email and find the Stallio reset message. Check spam if needed.
Follow the link to the reset page and choose a new password that meets the strength rules shown on signup.
Sign in at stallio.shop/login with the new password. If the link expired, request a fresh reset email.

cancel-or-change-plan.title: Cancel or change your subscription
cancel-or-change-plan.excerpt: Plans and billing cycles are shown on Pricing. Cancel or change through account messages and Contact when needed.
cancel-or-change-plan.intro: Stallio shows monthly and yearly options on Pricing. You can start without a card. Cancelling a paid monthly plan stops future charges; you keep access through the period already paid, as described on Pricing and the Refund Policy.
steps: Review current options on stallio.shop/pricing, including monthly and yearly billing.
If you are still in a free trial, you can stay on free features or subscribe when ready. You are not charged a subscription fee until you subscribe.
To cancel or change a paid plan, use the Contact page with subject Billing or plans, and include your account email and shop username.
Say clearly whether you want to cancel, move monthly to yearly, or the other way around.
After cancellation of a monthly plan, expect access to continue until the end of the period you already paid for, unless we confirm something different in writing.

billing-problems.title: Billing and payment problems
billing-problems.excerpt: Double charges, wrong amounts, and failed payments: what to gather and where to write.
billing-problems.intro: Subscription fees for seller plans are billed as described on Pricing. Shop orders between you and your customers are separate and are not Stallio subscription billing.
steps: Confirm the charge is a Stallio subscription fee, not a payout or payment you collected from a customer.
Note the charge date, amount, currency, and the email or shop username on the account.
For a possible billing mistake such as a double charge or billing after a confirmed cancellation, contact us within 30 days of the charge.
Use the Contact page, choose a billing-related subject, and include the details above.
If dashboard access was limited after a failed payment, mention that in the same note so we can connect billing and access.

request-refund.title: Request a subscription refund
request-refund.excerpt: Refunds follow the Refund Policy. Free plans have no subscription fee to refund.
request-refund.intro: This covers subscription fees you pay Stallio. It does not cover refunds for orders on your shop. Those stay between you and your customers.
steps: Read the Refund Policy so you know how monthly, yearly, free, and billing-mistake cases are handled.
Open the Contact page and include your account email, shop username, charge date, and a short description of the issue.
If you cancelled a monthly plan, remember unused days in a paid month are usually not refunded unless the law requires it or we confirm a billing mistake.
Yearly plans paid in advance are not automatically refunded for remaining months unless we confirm it in writing or local law requires it.
After we verify an approved refund, it is usually processed within 5 to 10 business days, depending on your payment provider.
